record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.original_question: Can the Bermond-Thomassen vertex-disjoint-cycles conjecture be verified for multipartite tournaments: does every multipartite tournament with minimum out-degree at least 2k - 1 contain k pairwise vertex-disjoint directed cycles?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.4 Verify Conjecture 3.3 for multipartite tournaments.
An orientation of a complete multipartite graph is called a multipartite tournament.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A multipartite tournament is an orientation of a complete multipartite graph: the vertex set is partitioned into independent classes, and between every two vertices in different classes there is exactly one directed edge (and no edges within a class). The minimum out-degree of a digraph D, denoted δ⁺(D), is the smallest out-degree over all its vertices. 

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every positive integer k, every multipartite tournament D with δ⁺(D) ≥ 2k − 1 contains k pairwise vertex-disjoint directed cycles.
artifact.status_search_result: The Bermond-Thomassen conjecture has been verified for tournaments (Bang-Jensen, Bessy, Thomassé) and for some subclasses of multipartite tournaments, including triangle-free multipartite tournaments and 3-partite tournaments. The full statement for arbitrary multipartite tournaments has not been established and recent work (e.g., a 2023 note on disjoint cycles in multipartite tournaments, and 2024 results on bipartite tournaments) continues to chip away at it. Hence the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Note on Disjoint Cycles in Multipartite Tournaments
status_evidence.snippet: Recent note providing partial progress on disjoint directed cycles in multipartite tournaments.
status_evidence.claim: Research on the Bermond–Thomassen conjecture restricted to multipartite tournaments is ongoing, with verification for sub-classes such as triangle-free and 3-partite tournaments.

status_evidence.title: Disjoint 3-Cycles in Tournaments: A Proof of The Bermond-Thomassen Conjecture for Tournaments
status_evidence.snippet: Bang-Jensen, Bessy and Thomassé prove the Bermond–Thomassen conjecture for tournaments.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture has been proved for tournaments, a special case of multipartite tournaments.

status_evidence.title: The Bermond-Thomassen Conjecture | Open Problem Garden
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the conjecture as still open in general.
status_evidence.claim: The general Bermond–Thomassen conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Disjoint cycles in tournaments and bipartite tournaments
status_evidence.snippet: 2024 paper providing further partial results in bipartite tournaments.
status_evidence.claim: The multipartite case continues to attract partial-result research.
